name: Minds Games
steps: Go to minds.games and choose "Claim a seat". Enter an email address and accept the campaign rules.

Verify a wallet by signing one message. The site says this involves no transaction and no gas. Warning A signature is all the wallet step needs. The rules say: "We will never ask for a seed phrase or private key." They also say wallet steps happen only on minds.games, so ignore links sent to you about the allowlist.

Create a Mind on HelloMinds, which is free, then use "Connect your Minds account" and approve the request so the site can map the Mind to your seat. Warning That approval gives minds.games access to your HelloMinds account. Read what the permission screen lists before you accept.
Watch @MindGames_AI on X for the allowlist results and the season dates. Neither had been published by 18 October 2026.
what: Minds Games has no token or airdrop. Its pre-season scoring locked on 12 October 2026 and its NFTs sold out. What is left, the $100,000 pool and the risks.
behind: The site names one person, by X handle: "BUILT BY @jesusislord". His X bio says he works on Anichess and builds at Animoca Brands. The site carries "Powered by" badges for HelloMinds and Checkmate. It names no company, and its domain was registered on 20 August 2026. costs: Signing up and scoring are free. Two things can cost money if you choose them: credits on HelloMinds, sold in packs of $10, $25 and $50, and a Minds NFT. The mint, at 0.0125 ETH, sold out on 14 October 2026, so a Mind can now only be bought from another holder at whatever price they ask. The top of the Minds Games homepage on 18 October 2026, with the headline, the $100,000 across 10 seasons line
risks: The site has no terms of service or privacy policy, although it collects your email address, wallet address and X profile. The $100,000 prize pool has no published rules, funder or payout terms. Rankings leaned heavily on referrals, so the top of the final table reflects who recruited the most people.
